review_type: original code-blind bounded Stormwood context catalogue rescore

reviewer.name: blind_listener_f10
reviewer.role: retained original independent code-blind visual judge

scope: New A/B/P/G context pixels only. Low Compatibility still-image judgments of the six requested supported rows; independent ratings against approved Stormwood boards and written ART_DIRECTION domain bar. No original 36 scores or 44-row catalogue changes.

scales.severity: 1–5; 1 is the required minimum for a bounded PASS with original defect not observed
scales.exposure: 1–5, independently rated recurrence/visibility of this subject in its pictured gameplay context
scales.importance: 1–5, independently rated consequence for readable player-facing presentation

rows.subject: named wild fight actor spacing
rows.reason: Voltarach, Sparkit and trainer have separate readable silhouettes in the sampled Hollows warning, opening and recovery views. Boss legs do not swallow Sparkit's body or the trainer in these full rasters; original crowding/intersection defect is not observed in this inspected subset.
limits: Still samples cannot establish collision clearance or all spacing during continuous motion, other party formations or four-player combat.
Severity 1 is the requested scale minimum; it does not assert a residual observed spacing defect.

rows.subject: named wild danger and opening cues
rows.reason: The broad magenta warning wedge disappears at the sampled impact, but a bright magenta warning-shaped glyph/sector remains beneath Voltarach while the HUD says 'it's open — hit it'. It is absent in the recovery sample. The localized residual still creates conflicting warning/opening semantics; this is smaller than the broad pre-impact hazard and does not obscure Sparkit's whole silhouette.
limits: Chronological stills support coexistence and sampled disappearance only; they do not prove cue duration, input windows or continuous timing.
No implementation or purpose of the residual glyph is inferred.

rows.subject: shared fight tell and hit effects
rows.reason: The warning uses a flat saturated magenta wedge/ring with a central glyph, while opening is communicated prominently through HUD text. In the Mosshock hit sample a large pale-yellow faceted circular graphic covers central upper-body detail, reducing the readable hit silhouette. The supplied stills retain visible creature bodies, but the effects do not meet the written object-first, weighted hit-feedback bar.
limits: Supported for inspected Voltarach tells and one Mosshock hit graphic, not every move/effect archetype or every encounter.
Hitstop, knockback weight, animation timing, sound and continuous response cannot be rated from these stills.

rows.subject: fight team roster contrast
rows.reason: In the Hollows start, impact and recovery full rasters the five-row roster above the active card is extremely transparent: terrain and grass overpower its header, icons and bars. The active Sparkit card remains readable. The Mosshock hit view has a substantially clearer roster, so the observed defect is context-dependent rather than uniformly present.
limits: No physical 7-inch display test or measured contrast ratio is claimed.
These are pictured combat backgrounds; all background/preset combinations are not exposed.

rows.subject: dialogue foreground obstruction
rows.reason: Ondra's face and upper body remain clearly visible even with a very large foreground Sparkit at the left edge. Fenn remains visible beside a large trunk and shrubs. The inspected people contact views similarly keep named speakers visible above the dialogue panel; the original foreground-companion/overhead obstruction is not observed in these staged conversation views.
limits: The dialogue panel intentionally covers the lower body; this is distinct from a creature or overhead object hiding the speaker.
No earned interaction, moving companion configurations or universal dialogue-camera coverage is claimed.
Severity 1 is the requested scale minimum; it does not assert a residual observed obstruction defect.

rows.subject: Glass Sink landmark
rows.reason: All four supplied approach/close views show a grassy rim abruptly ending above a very broad gray, repetitively gridded lower surface. A height drop is visible, but no distinct localized sink form or recognizable glass/crystalline material establishes the named landmark. The near views retain the same unmarked grass-to-void transition rather than revealing authored rim/detail identity.
limits: All four G full rasters were inspected; these two headings and their day/golden labels are not a complete rim, route or phase matrix.
Day/golden labels do not establish a Stormwood day/night cycle; both pictured views retain the purple storm sky.
The still images establish visible landmark-shape/material failure only; no reachability, collision, depth measurement or traversal mechanism is inferred.

withheld_rows.subject: Hollows fight loss result clarity
withheld_rows.missing_context: Actual natural Hollows defeat and ensuing loss/out-of-fight result. Requested fixture levels/names are not outcomes; disclosed forced-cleanup A/B 99-after and 100-aftermath views are excluded.

withheld_rows.missing_context: Actual natural Hollows victory acknowledgement, reward tiles and persistent quickbar together. Requested fixture levels/names are not outcomes; disclosed forced-cleanup A/B 99-after and 100-aftermath views are excluded.
